title: Saline versus alkaline stresses in paddy soils drive divergent microbial nutrient limitations despite shared carbon constraints
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Soil salinization and alkalization often suppress microbial functional activity, triggering negative feedback loops in microbial metabolism, degrading nutrients and agricultural productivity. However, the impacts of saline versus alkaline soils on microbial metabolism remain unclear. We compared reclaimed coastal saline (S 1) and Songnen alkaline (A 1) paddy soils with their corresponding non-saline controls (S 0 and A 0) using models of ecoenzymatic stoichiometry, aggregate fractionation, amplicon sequencing and high-throughput qPCR to quantify microbial carbon (C), nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) limitation and their abiotic and biotic drivers. Our findings revealed that saline and alkaline stresses consistently intensified microbial C limitation by 24.79% and 90.43%, respectively, relative to their corresponding CK soils. However, the two regional soil systems showed divergent nutrient limitation patterns associated with contrasting physicochemical and microbial conditions. Saline soils exhibited acute microbial N limitation (VTN/P limitation = −6.51), which was associated with lower N availability, including 53.29% lower DTN than in alkaline soils, macroaggregate-associated N depletion, and bacterial-associated network reorganization. Microbial functional profiles further indicated greater genetic potential for denitrification and lower genetic potential for dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium, with A 1 soils having 25.12% lower nirK/S abundance and 49.68% higher napA abundance than S 1 soils. In contrast, alkaline soils exhibited stronger microbial P limitation (VTN/P limitation = 9.73), which was associated with reduced P bioavailability, including 56.68% lower AP than in saline soils, greater P sequestration in silt+clay fractions, and fungal-associated network reorganization. This pattern was accompanied by stronger suppression of genes associated with organic P mineralization and inorganic P solubilization, with phnK and gcd + pqqC abundances being 28.27% and 25.19% lower than in S 1 soils, respectively. These results show that divergent microbial nutrient limitations arise from coupled soil physicochemical constraints, microbial community reassembly, network reorganization and functional gene responses, rather than from ion-specific chemistry alone. These results highlight organic matter restoration as a common priority, but indicate divergent N/P fertilization strategies for saline and alkaline soils. These insights provide a fundamental framework for targeted remediation of saline and alkaline soils and facilitate sustainable agricultural practices by integrating both universal and salt-type-specific methodological approaches.

摘要

土壤盐渍化和碱化通常会抑制微生物功能活性，引发微生物代谢的负反馈效应，进而导致土壤养分状况恶化和农业生产力下降。然而，盐胁迫与碱胁迫对土壤微生物代谢的影响及其差异仍不明确。 本研究以滨海盐土(S1)和松嫩平原碱土(A1)改良稻田及其对应的非盐碱对照土壤(S0和A0)为研究对象，综合运用生态酶化学计量学模型、土壤团聚体分级、扩增子测序和高通量荧光定量PCR等方法，定量评估土壤微生物碳(C)、氮(N)和磷(P)限制特征，并解析其非生物和生物驱动因素。 研究结果表明，与各自对照土壤相比，盐胁迫和碱胁迫均显著加剧了微生物碳限制，增幅分别为24.79%和90.43%。然而，由于土壤理化性质和微生物特征存在差异，两类土壤系统表现出截然不同的养分限制模式。滨海盐土表现出强烈的微生物氮限制(VTN/P limitation = −6.51)，这与较低的氮素有效性密切相关，具体表现为溶解性总氮(DTN)含量较碱土降低53.29%、大团聚体中氮素亏缺以及细菌相关网络重组。微生物功能特征进一步表明，盐土中反硝化过程的遗传潜力较高，而硝酸盐异化还原成铵(DNRA)的遗传潜力较低。其中，与S1土壤相比，A1土壤中nirK/S基因丰度降低25.12%，而napA基因丰度增加49.68%。相比之下，碱土表现出更强的微生物磷限制(VTN/P limitation = 9.73)，这与磷生物有效性降低密切相关，具体表现为有效磷(AP)含量较盐土降低56.68%、粉砂和黏粒组分中磷固定增强以及真菌相关网络重组。同时，碱土中参与有机磷矿化和无机磷溶解的功能基因受到更强抑制，其中phnK和gcd + pqqC基因丰度分别较S1土壤降低28.27%和25.19%。这些结果表明，盐土与碱土中不同的微生物养分限制模式并非仅由特定盐离子的化学性质决定，而是土壤理化条件约束、微生物群落重组、网络结构重构及功能基因响应共同作用的结果。 本研究强调，有机质恢复是盐土和碱土改良的共同优先措施，但两类土壤应采取差异化的氮、磷养分管理策略。研究结果为结合共性改良措施与盐分类型特异性调控途径，实现盐土和碱土的精准修复及农业可持续利用提供了重要的理论依据。
